geo_headlines: DEMOCRATS WIN BOTH CHAMBERS. **Democrats took control of the Senate and the House, flipping Senate seats in Texas, Ohio, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Maine; Trump said he will accept the results (CNN, NBC, Economic Times).** CNBC projects at least 54 Democratic Senate seats. Divided government from January means subpoena power and a check on the White House agenda.

FUTURES: A ROUND TRIP. Nasdaq 100 futures fell as much as 2.4% and S&P 500 futures 1.4% as results came in, then recovered (Reuters). Now S&P futures 7,671 (+1.0%) and Nasdaq 100 futures 28,560.75 (+0.9%), led by AMD after hours. Trump Media -7% and SpaceX -4.5% premarket (Benzinga).

IRAN: STRIKE PLANS VS TALKS. US media report Central Command has plans ready for strikes that could begin as early as today, with three carriers in the region. Trump called Monday's Qeshm strike minor and said it wasn't war. Iran called the US reply to its seven conditions not convincing, while Qatar says it is relaying proposals in real time (Al Jazeera).

HORMUZ AND TEHRAN'S MESSAGE. The IRGC said four tankers were destroyed after hitting mines on a prohibited route south of the strait (Reuters). Parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Americans voted no to war and Iran endorses that message (ABC).

GOLD JUMPS, OIL SLIPS. Gold $4,052.30 (+2.8%), back above $4,000. January Brent $102.37 (-1.2%) after Tuesday's $103.60 settle, the lowest in nearly four weeks; December WTI $95.37 (-0.7%) (Benzinga). Bitcoin $78,490 (+1.5%). FedWatch: December hike odds 80.4%, up from 73.4%.

client_frame_short: The election delivered a clean result: Democrats won both the House and the Senate, so Washington moves to divided government in January. Futures dropped on the news overnight, then fully recovered, and are now up about 1%, helped by strong AMD results. **Divided government has historically been fine for markets because it limits big policy swings; the bigger near-term risk is still Iran, where US strike plans are reportedly ready as early as today.** For clients: no portfolio changes for an election result; stay diversified.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the headline is the election, but the market risk this week is still Iran.

What changed overnight: Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House, flipping Senate seats in states such as Texas, Ohio, Kansas and South Carolina. From January, Washington moves to divided government, which means more oversight, more gridlock, and fewer sweeping policy changes. Futures fell sharply as results came in, with Nasdaq futures down as much as 2.4%, then recovered completely; S&P 500 futures are now up about 1%. AMD helped, guiding for 80% revenue growth next year. Gold jumped almost 3% back above $4,000.

Iran: US media report that strike plans are ready as early as today, with three aircraft carriers in the region. Iran called the latest US reply not convincing, while Qatar says it is relaying proposals between the two sides in real time. Oil slipped about 1%, so traders are not pricing a big escalation yet.

Where we stand: the S&P 500 rose 0.4% Tuesday and is about 3.2% below its October 6 record close. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.95%, and futures markets now see an 80% chance of a December rate hike, up from 73%.

Why it matters: markets have historically done well under divided government; gridlock reduces policy surprises. The real swing factor is whether strikes resume and push oil and inflation fears higher. The new Congress is not seated until January, so nothing changes in fiscal or trade policy before then; expect hearings and headlines, not new laws, in the near term.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and avoid election or Iran-headline trades in either direction. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Tuesday 4.95%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Tuesday 5.32%), or US strikes that resume full combat and keep Brent well above $105 (now $102.37).
